ex-divisor-rational-function-projective-.notes: The chart calculation uses t,t−1,u as uniformizers and f=t²/(t−1)=1/[u(1−u)] at infinity, giving orders +2,−1,−1; all other height-one primes avoid t(t−1). The support and zero/pole sign are correct.

ex-principal-divisor-degree-zero-p1.notes: Coprime polynomial factorization gives finite-point valuations a_i and −b_j; the u-chart yields infinity order n−m. Residue degrees equal polynomial degrees, so the weighted total is m−n+n−m=0, including constant polynomials.

def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-gro.notes: DC and local finiteness license the finite principal sum. Valuation additivity makes principal divisors a subgroup of Div(X), and Cl(X) is the quotient; no-prime-divisor and constant-unit cases are explicit.

lem-pullback-cartier-divisor-line-bundle.notes: Admissible equations give pulled-back generators with exactly the same unit transition functions, so local line-bundle maps glue and are datum-independent. For effective D the canonical section 1 maps to 1; empty cases are included.

cex-pullback-weil-divisor-undefined.notes: The closed-point map Spec k→A1 sends the regular equation t to the zero meromorphic function, which is neither a regular section nor a meromorphic unit. Its inverse-image closed scheme has codimension zero and source has no prime divisors; the example refutes unrestricted equation pullback, without denying the zero Weil group.

cex-zero-divisor-equation-not-cartier.notes: In the dual-numbers local ring, every generator aε of (ε) is annihilated by nonzero ε. Thus the locally principal closed point has no regular local equation and is not effective Cartier; the one-point topology licenses the single-chart check.

lem-global-section-effective-divisor.notes: Local coefficients of a global section are regular iff O→L by that section is injective; change of trivialization multiplies them by units. They form an effective Cartier datum and the generator map O(D)→L sends 1 to s. The remark now correctly says a regular section is not identically zero on a nonempty open, while it may vanish at points.

thm-line-bundle-rational-section-cartier.notes: Read the whole current proof and Cartier sheaf/rational-section prerequisites. On integral X, coefficients of a nonzero rational section are nonzero in K(X) and transition by regular units. Generator maps f^-1 -> e glue; their meromorphic extensions carry 1_D to s. For D=-[0] on Spec k[t], O(D)=t O_X excludes 1 as a regular section, so F4 and step 5.1 now explicitly type 1_D as rational. It is regular precisely for effective D. Stacks 31.15.1(2) is limited to effective divisors; the arbitrary-divisor argument follows from the actual local formula.

ex-divisor-cusp-normalization-pullback.notes: The cusp ring k[t²,t³] is a domain whose normalization is k[t], because t is integral and k[t] is integrally closed. The regular equation x=t² pulls back to t², of valuation 2 at the origin and 0 elsewhere; line-bundle pullback matches 1. Nonnormality is correctly confined to the vertex; A_x=k[t,t^{-1}] is normal.

lem-cartier-to-weil-respects-principal-a.notes: At each height-one generic point, multiplying local Cartier equations adds DVR valuations, so cyc is additive and sends div_C(f) to div_W(f). lem-cartier-to-weil-injective-normal.notes: On a normal Noetherian integral affine chart, a Cartier equation of zero cycle has zero valuation at every height-one prime; the AC-backed S2 intersection puts both it and its inverse in the coordinate ring, hence it is a unit. thm-cartier-weil-isomorphism-locally-fac.notes: Local UFDs are integrally closed, so the Noetherian integral scheme is normal. A height-one prime in each local UFD is principal; finite generation spreads its generator to a neighbourhood, making each prime divisor effective Cartier with cycle coefficient 1 at itself and 0 elsewhere. Finite Weil sums give cycle surjectivity; the AC-backed normal injectivity lemma gives an isomorphism and Pic≅Cl. Empty, zero and negative divisor boundaries are stated.

cor-degree-descends-picard-curve.notes: A normal proper integral curve has field generic stalk and DVR closed-point stalks, hence is locally factorial. The Cartier–Weil/Picard–class isomorphism and zero degree of principals make the weighted degree descend to a homomorphism Pic(C)→Z. The false remark that principals exhaust the degree kernel was removed; degree-zero nonprincipal classes can occur, as Stacks §53.17 shows for positive genus.
